Liskiava Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Alytus County, Lithuania

Not demolished. Jews first settled in Liškiava in the early 18th century at the invitation of Dominican monks seeking to develop the settlement; by 1761 Jews owned 11 of the village's 16 houses. The population grew to 170 by 1821, reaching about a third of the village's 613 residents by 1897, and 146 (36 percent) by the 1923 Lithuanian census. About 10 Jewish families remained at the time of the 1940 Soviet occupation; after the German invasion, Liškiava's Jews were taken to Merkinė and murdered there.
